dedupe_keys.name: curblr open data specification for curb regulations using linear referencing

description: CurbLR is an open data standard for describing curb regulations, meaning who may park, load, stop or pick up passengers along each stretch of kerb, at what times and at what price. It was created by SharedStreets after reviewing the parking regulation datasets of several US cities and converting about 35,000 Los Angeles parking zones, and is kept as an open specification on GitHub. Coverage: generic standard, used in North American curb inventories and pilot projects. A CurbLR feed is a GeoJSON feature collection in which each feature references a street segment by linear referencing (a SharedStreets reference ID plus the location along it) and carries regulations: the activity allowed or banned, user classes such as taxis or permit holders, time spans by day and hour, and payment rates. Format and access: specification, JSON schema and examples on GitHub, with tools built by others for mapping curbs and converting inventories; free. Licence: the specification is CC0 and the code MIT. Caveats: the repository has been quiet since December 2020, the newer Curb Data Specification from the Open Mobility Foundation now covers similar ground, and the standard carries no data of its own. Simulation uses: encoding curb space and its rules for agent-based models of parking, deliveries and ride-hailing pick-ups and for capacity planning of street space. Related records: the San Francisco automated vehicle curbside study (case_study-san-francisco-cbd-av-curbside-sumo) models the same kind of curb activity.
